chunks: 14 - Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim. He said: Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to me, from Sufyan, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Habib ibn al-Jahm. He said:

When Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) departed with us to the land of Siffin, he stopped in a village called Sanduda'. Then he ordered us and we turned away from it. Then he encamped with us at night in a barren land. So Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar rose and said: O Commander of the Faithful, do you make the people camp without water?! He said: O Malik, indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, will give us to drink in this place water sweeter than honey, softer than pure butter, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby. So we were amazed, though there is no amazement at the words of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Then he came forward dragging his cloak, with his sword in his hand, until he stood on the barren land. He said: O Malik, dig - you and your companions. So Malik said: We dug and found a great black rock with a ring gleaming like silver. He said to us: Try to move it. So we tried with all of us - and we were a hundred men - but we could not move it from its place. Then the Commander of the Faithful drew near, raising his hand to the sky in supplication, saying: Tab tab Marya Alam tibu Thabutha Shamthiya Kuba Hahanu Thatu Dithabar Hutha - Amen, amen, O Lord of the Worlds, Lord of Musa and Harun. Then he seized it and hurled it forty cubits from the spring. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar said: Water appeared to us, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby. We drank and gave others to drink. Then he replaced the rock and ordered us to heap earth upon it. Then he departed. We had not gone far when he said: Which of you knows the location of the spring? We said: All of us, O Commander of the Faithful. So we returned and searched for the spring, but its location was hidden from us most extremely. We thought that the Commander of the Faithful was overcome by thirst, so we looked around and found the hermitage of a monk. We approached it and found a monk whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes from old age. We said: O monk, do you have water with which we might give our master to drink? He said: I have water that I purified two days ago. He brought down to us water that was bitter and rough. We said: This is what you purified two days ago! How would it be if you had drunk from the water that our master gave us? And we told him about the matter. He said: Is this master of yours a prophet? We said: No, but he is the deputy of a prophet. So he came down to us after his wariness of us, and said: Take me to your master. So we took him, and when the Commander of the Faithful saw him, he said: Sham'un? The monk said: Yes, Sham'un. This is the name my mother gave me. No one knew it except God, blessed and exalted, and now you. So how did you know it? Complete it so I may complete it for you. He said: What do you wish, O Sham'un? He said: This spring and its name. He said: This is the spring of Rahuma, and it is from Paradise. Three hundred and thirteen deputies have drunk from it, and I am the last of the deputies to drink from it. The monk said: This is what I found in all the books of the Gospel, and I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that you are the deputy of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Then the Commander of the Faithful departed, and the monk went before him until he reached Siffin and camped with him among the devout. When the two ranks met, the first one to receive martyrdom was the monk. The Commander of the Faithful dismounted with his eyes shedding tears and said: A person is with whom he loves. The monk is with us on the Day of Resurrection, and he is my companion in Paradise.

key_terms.بلقع: Barren, desolate land - an uninhabited wasteland without water or vegetation
key_terms.راحوما: Rahuma - the name of the spring from Paradise that 313 deputies drank from
key_terms.شمعون: Sham'un (Simeon) - the monk's hidden name, revealed by Imam Ali through divine knowledge
key_terms.صفين: Siffin - the location of the famous battle between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya in 37 AH
key_terms.صومعة: Hermitage - a monastic cell or tower where a monk lives in seclusion
key_terms.وصي: Deputy/successor (wasi) - the one entrusted with carrying on the Prophet's mission

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Imam Ali perform with the hidden spring during the march to Siffin?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts a miraculous event during Imam Ali's march to the Battle of Siffin (37 AH). In a barren land, Imam Ali revealed a hidden spring called Rahuma by lifting a massive rock that a hundred men could not move, after reciting a supplication in what appears to be Syriac/Aramaic. A Christian monk named Sham'un, astonished by the miracle and Imam Ali's knowledge of his secret name, embraced Islam after learning the spring was from Paradise and that 313 deputies had drunk from it. The monk joined Ali's army and was the first martyr at Siffin, prompting Ali to declare the prophetic saying that a person will be with whom he loves.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim. He said: Abu’l Salt `Abd al-Salam b. Salih narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to me from Sufyan from al-Awza`i from Yahya b. Abi Kathir from Habib b. al-Jahm. He said:

When `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) went with us to the land of Siffin, he disembarked in a village called Sanduda’. Then, he ordered us to come to it. Then, he disembarked with us at night in a barren land. So, Malik b. al-Harith al-Ashtar went to him and said: O Amir al-Mu’minin (as)! Why would you cause the people to disembark in a place that does not have water?! So, he said: O Malik! Surely, Allah will feed us water that is purer than honey, softer than butter, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby. So, we became astonished; and there is nothing more astonishing than the words of Amir al-Mu’minin (as). Then, he began to drag his cloak, with his sword in his hand, until he stood on the barren land. He said: O Malik – you and your companions, dig. So, Malik said: We dug until we found a great black rock with a ring that shone like silver. So, he said to us: Throw it. So, we tried to throw it – and we had one hundred men gathered – but we could not move it from its place. So, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) came forward with his hands raised to the sky, supplicating and saying: … amen, amen O Lord of the Worlds, Lord of Musa and Harun. Then, he took it and hurled it forty armlengths away from a river. Malik b. al-Harith al-Ashtar said: Then, water that was purer than honey, softer than butter, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby appeared to us. We drank from it and fed from it. Then, he returned the rock, and ordered us to throw dust atop it. Then, we continued when, not far away, he said: Which of you know the location of the river? So, we said: All of us, O Amir al-Mu’minin. So, we returned, and we looked for the river, but it had been extremely hidden from us. So, we thought that Amir al-Mu’minin (as) was overburdened with thirst, so we went out and found the hermitage of a monk. We approached it until we found a monk whose eyebrows covered his eyes from old age. So, we said: O monk! Do you have water that we could feed our master with? He said: I have water that I purified two days ago. So, he brought us water that was bitter and rough. We said: Is this what you purified two days ago?! How would you be if you had drunk from the water that our master had given us? So, we told him about the matter, and he said: Is this master of yours a prophet? We said: No, but he is the deputy of a prophet. So, he came down to us after his absence and said: Take me to your master. So, we took him, and when Amir al-Mu’minin (as) saw him, he said: Sham`un? The monk said: Yes, Sham`un, this is the name that my mother gave me. No one knows this except Allah, and now you, so how did you find out? He said: What do you want, Sham`un? He said: This river and its name. He said: This river is Rahuma, and it is from Paradise. Three hundred and thirteen deputies have drunk from it, and I am the last deputy to drink from it. So, the monk said: This is what I found in all the books of the Gospel, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that you are the deputy of Muhammad (s). Then, the monk went with Amir al-Mu’minin (as) until he reached Siffin. The monk was among the first to be martyred. So, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) went down with his eyes saddened, saying: A person will be with whom he loves. The monk will be with us on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be my friend in Paradise.
